_note: SPACE CARGO 2: THE SEALED DELIVERY. Collect a sealed container in one orbit and deliver it to a station.
THE HOOK: nobody tells you what's in it, and the woman receiving it is all business until it's opened. It's soil
from Earth, sealed by her grandmother the year they left. Earth is named in the JOURNAL only; the voice says 'the
NEEDS A SECOND ORBIT: the station is over another planet. boardspace has one orbit today, so the deliver sits in the
same cell until Eliza prices a second (her 'an ORBIT third place may sit beside a second request').

NEEDS ONE NEW OBJECT: a ship or station static to DELIVER to in orbit (every orbit deliver so far is a satellite). One ask covers 36a, 37a and 39a; the model string is a stand-in (the lint does not catch it), picked by him or Kim.

Every space Delve before these was a satellite (5 of 7); these are about CARGO, his ask. Markers: General01/06/02 and TravelB02 are 51a's and 30a's; which a cell offers is Eliza's. No names, places, factions or currency in a voiced line. Pay: med, capped, placeholder.

prose.name: Hauling: Sealed Container over <Planet>
prose.briefing: A sealed container is waiting in orbit over <Planet> for a courier who won't ask what's in it. The receiving end is a station.
prose.card: Local Contract. Deliver a sealed container over <Planet> to the receiving station unopened. Payment on contract completion.

beats.journal: The container's seal is older than anything else on it, and it's light for its size. I'm not to open it. I need to deliver it to the station.
beats.name: Sealed Container
say: It's aboard. Bring it in slowly, I'll be waiting at the dock.

beats.objective: Deliver the container to the station
beats.journal: I delivered the sealed container. It held a jar of soil from Earth, sealed before anyone left, and the woman who received it went very quiet.
beats._model: A small station static in orbit, not boardable. His or Kim's pick.
beats.name: Receiving Station

message.title: Container Delivered
message.text: The seal breaks with a long hiss. Inside is a single jar of dark soil, labelled by hand.

say: It's soil. From the first home, from before. My grandmother sealed it the year they left, and I have never once seen it opened.

broadcast: The container's sealed and it stays that way. Collect it and bring it to the station, and please don't fly like you're in a hurry, because it can't be replaced.
_speech: Businesslike until the last line. Annie K, heard on 32a; his ear decides.
